sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows bilateral thickened and enhancing fallopian tubes . A moderate amount of free pelvic fluid is also present.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-04

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Transvaginal color Doppler ultrasound in a 23-year-old woman with pelvic pain shows a thickened fallopian tube . Note the thickened fimbrial end of the tube . There is a small amount of fluid surrounding the fimbrial end of the tube.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-06

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT in a patient with pyosalpinx shows a tubular left adnexal structure with thick, enhancing walls and inflammation of the adjacent pelvic fat . Separate left ovary is not shown.

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Coronal CECT shows bilateral, fluid-filled, tubular adnexal masses with a thickened, hypervascular wall. The ovaries are separate (not shown). There is surrounding pelvic fat stranding and free peritoneal fluid .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-09

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Coronal CECT in the same patient shows fluid distention of the uterine cavity and hyperenhancement of the endometrium , consistent with endometritis. Salpingitis and pyosalpinx are due to ascending infection; therefore, endometritis and oophoritis may also be seen.

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Transvaginal ultrasound in a 43-year-old woman who presented with fever and pelvic pain shows a complex, nonspecific, solid, and cystic left adnexal mass .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-11

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T2 FSE MR in the same patient shows the left tuboovarian abscess with fluid centrally and a thick, irregular wall . sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-13

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T1 C+ FS MR shows the thick rim enhancement typical of a tuboovarian abscess. Note mesh-like stranding in pelvic fat. Normal ovarian or fallopian tube architecture has been destroyed by the advanced infection.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-14

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows a large, complex, cystic adnexal mass with thick wall and septal enhancement , consistent with a tuboovarian abscess. There is no normal separate ovary.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-15

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Coronal CECT in the same patient shows best the inflammation surrounding this large tuboovarian abscess .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-16

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T2 MR in a 37-year-old woman who presented with pelvic pain and fever shows a solid and cystic left ovarian mass , demonstrating multiple fluid-filled loculi separated by thick septa and a right ovarian mass demonstrating fluid-fluid level and T2 shading. sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-17

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T1 MR in the same patient shows a left ovarian mass demonstrating low signal intensity and a unilocular right ovarian mass , which demonstrates high signal intensity and represents endometrioma.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-18

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Coronal T2 MR in the same patient shows a solid and cystic left ovarian mass and a unilocular right ovarian mass . Note endometriotic fibrous band connecting the back of the uterus to the right ovary.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-19

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial DWI b800 MR (above) and ADC map (below) demonstrate high signal intensity of a fluid loculus on DWI sequence and low signal intensity on the ADC map due to diffusion restriction. sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-20

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T1 C+ FS MR in the same patient shows a left ovarian multilocular mass with enhancing wall and septa. Note also the irregular enhancing streaks within the pelvic fat .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-21

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T1 C+ FS MR in the same patient shows a left ovarian multilocular mass with enhancing wall and septa. Note also the enhancing peritoneum .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-22

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T2 MR in a 41-year-old woman who presented with pelvic pain and fever shows a unilocular cystic left ovarian mass with an intermediate signal intensity thick wall.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-23

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T1 MR in the same patient shows a left ovarian mass demonstrating low signal intensity. There is a characteristic hyperintense rim along the inner wall of abscess cavity due to granulation tissue and hemorrhage.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-24

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial DWI b800 MR in the same patient demonstrates increased signal intensity of the cystic component due to diffusion restriction. sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T1 C+ FS MR in the same patient shows a left ovarian unilocular cystic mass with thick, enhancing wall.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-26

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT in a 31-year-old woman shows an enlarged right ovary containing multiple peripherally enhancing fluid collections due to tuboovarian abscess.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-27

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT in the same patient shows thickening and enhancement of the anterior liver capsule due to Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome, which results from peritoneal spread of infection via the right paracolic gutter to involve peritoneal surfaces of the right upper quadrant (RUQ), resulting in perihepatitis (inflammation of Glisson capsule).
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-28

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT in a patient with a tuboovarian abscess shows diffuse wall thickening of a nondistended gallbladder. There is free fluid in the hepatorenal fossa .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-29

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Coronal CECT in the same patient shows the right tuboovarian abscess with inflammation extending along the ovarian vascular pedicle . sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-30

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT through the pelvis in a 28-year-old woman with Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome, severe pelvic inflammatory disease, and abnormal liver function tests shows bilateral, thick-walled tuboovarian abscesses .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-31

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT through the upper abdomen in the same patient shows periportal edema and regional perfusion abnormalities due to perihepatitis from peritoneal spread of infection.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-32

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT in a 55-year-old woman with recently diagnosed diverticulitis shows right ovarian peripherally enhancing fluid collections communicating with a pericolonic abscess .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-33

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Coronal CECT in the same patient shows right ovarian peripherally enhancing fluid collections communicating with a sigmoid pericolonic abscess . sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-34

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T2 MR in a 38-year-old woman with history of renal transplant who presented with pelvic pain and fever shows a multilocular cystic left ovarian mass with a smooth wall. There is a walled-off fluid collection anterior to the left ovary .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-35

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T2 MR in the same patient shows a multilocular cystic left ovarian mass with an intermediate signal intensity thick wall. There is a walled-off fluid collection surrounding the left ovary.

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial DWI b800 MR in the same patient demonstrates increased signal intensity of the larger cystic component and a smaller posterior locule due to diffusion restriction. There is also a high signal intensity, walled-off fluid collection anterior to the left ovary.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-37

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial ADC map in the same patient shows low signal intensity of the larger locule and the satellite locule due to diffusion restriction. The walled-off fluid collection shows high signal intensity due to T2 shine-through phenomenon.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-38

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T1 FS MR in the same patient shows a left ovarian abscess with its fluid content demonstrating low signal intensity. There is a characteristic hyperintense rim along the inner wall of abscess cavity due to granulation tissue and hemorrhage.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-39

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T1 C+ FS MR in the same patient shows a left ovarian cystic mass with a thick, enhancing wall.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-40

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Transabdominal pelvic ultrasound in a 26-year-old woman who presented with pelvic pain and fever shows a multilocular, solid, cystic right ovarian mass with thick, irregular wall and multiple septa. sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-41

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T2 MR in the same patient shows a multilocular, cystic right ovarian mass with a thick, irregular wall and multiple septa separating the cavity into multiple irregular locules.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-42

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial DWI b800 MR in the same patient demonstrates increased signal intensity of the right ovarian abscess .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-43

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial ADC map in the same patient shows low signal intensity of the multilocular right ovarian abscess due to diffusion restriction.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-44

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T1 MR in the same patient shows a right ovarian abscess with its fluid content demonstrating low signal intensity. Also notice the characteristic hyperintense rim along the inner wall of abscess cavities due to granulation tissue and hemorrhage.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-45

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T1 C+ FS MR in the same patient shows a right ovarian cystic mass with a thick, irregular enhancing wall and septa.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-46

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Sagittal endovaginal grayscale ultrasound shows oophoritis in early pelvic inflammatory disease with marked enlargement of the ovary and prominent cystic areas within ovarian parenchyma .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-47

CORE GAP CONFIRMED (User-declared). Core was excluded from card content and provenance; no Core Summary or Core-derived cards were generated. The previously reviewed uploaded Core PDF was therefore not used as a card source for this build.

Whole-source coverage audit completed from the full RadPrimer + STATdx package under the Core GAP pathway. SECTION A cardinality passed: 27 provided case clusters → 27 eligible → 0 excluded → exactly 27 PRIMARY UNKNOWN cards. The selected-image audit also passed: 58/58 source-qualified primary images are accounted for.

Final deck composition is 54 cards: 27 UNKNOWN, 5 Differential Drills, 1 Definition, 4 Mechanism, 4 Boards Trap, 1 Epidemiology, and 12 non-epidemiology High-Yield cards. The TSV has exactly 54 physical lines × 22 columns, no header, an empty Tags column on every row, no literal newlines inside fields, and the summary uses ASCII-safe HTML numeric icon references. Image_Annotated and Original_Caption were intentionally left blank because your architecture makes them optional; this avoids altering any supplied caption while retaining the source-qualified image filenames and caption-derived keyword findings.

The required external diagnostic-performance review was also performed. The available systematic-review evidence for CT/MRI diagnostic accuracy in acute PID was judged uncertain/very uncertain, so I did not create a performance card from unstable external numbers. PubMed+1

Total cards to export: 54. Expected TSV lines: 54.
